title: Continuous genealogy risk caps and online residual-frequency calibration improve some transients but do not robustly dominate a fixed defensive reserve

public_sources.title: Model-Agnostic Online Certificate-Driven Calibration for Time Series Forecasting Under Distribution Shift
public_sources.authors: Chenfeng Huang, Zixuan Ma, George Michailidis
public_sources.use: Finite-sample martingale certificates under temporal dependence and shift, with a gated corrective head that reverts to a fixed backbone and a predict-then-update protocol. This suggests a certificate-gated defensive-backbone design; it is not a theorem for the particle-allocation model here.

public_sources.title: Online Conformal Prediction via Online Optimization
public_sources.authors: Felipe Areces, Christopher Mohri, Tatsunori Hashimoto, John Duchi
public_sources.use: Provides adversarial time-average coverage and, under a linear conditional-quantile assumption, stochastic conditional coverage convergence. It supports treating residual calibration as its own frequency/conditional-quantile layer rather than a run-level variance certificate.

public_sources.title: Online Conformal Prediction for Non-Exchangeable Panel Data
public_sources.use: A two-state online conformal design gives a stepwise coverage bound and long-run guarantee using contemporaneous related-unit calibration plus target feedback. The contemporaneous-panel structure is absent in the present particle model, so the stepwise result is not transferred.

public_sources.title: Adaptive online variance estimation in particle filters: the ALVar estimator
public_sources.use: Remains a strong single-run online genealogy-variance reference under its stated particle-filter/resampling assumptions. A targeted search in this run did not establish a theorem-clean generation-wise estimator specifically for the independent-stratified multi-generation implementation used here.

synthetic_model.reference: Same 12-generation two-state Feynman-Kac model, independent stratified resampling, 768 particles/run, exact post-hoc A scoring, continuation CV^2 coefficient proxy and lag-4 genealogy localizer as r125-r126.
synthetic_model.implementation_crosscheck: Fresh reproduction matched the prior benchmark regime closely: on an independent 8-stream smoke set, uncertainty allocation gave mean ratios about 0.8524/0.8124/0.8652 and fixed beta=0.5 about 0.8874/0.8575/0.8754 for abrupt/gradual/recurring, respectively.

continuous_risk_controller.risk_definition: After a completed run, normalize lag-4 genealogy increments only to identify the dominant generation and localization confidence c=1-second/top. Set localization strength max(0,(c-0.3)/(1-0.3)); multiply by min(1,|genealogy_argmax-pre_run_continuation_argmax|/3). No genealogy magnitude is used as A.
continuous_risk_controller.memory_and_cap: risk_memory <- max(risk_raw,0.95*risk_memory); beta_max=0.5+0.4*exp(-8*risk_memory). The ordinary r125 uncertainty-box controller chooses beta on its grid and is then capped by beta_max.
continuous_risk_controller.discovery: 64 frozen candidates over c0 in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4}, k in {4,6,8,12}, decay in {0.5,0.7,0.85,0.95}, 4 streams/scenario. The selected candidate minimized mean exact ratio plus an explicit transient and risk-duty penalty. Validation below used disjoint seed families and no retuning.
continuous_risk_controller.interpretation: The continuous cap sharply reduced the uncertainty controller's recurring worst transient (1.3170 to 1.1700) and improved average efficiency versus fixed beta=0.5 in abrupt and gradual stress, but it was slightly worse than fixed beta in recurring mean and materially worse in recurring worst transient. Risk remained nontrivially active most of the time, showing that noisy genealogy disagreement plus slow memory behaves too much like a persistent moderate clamp. This candidate is not adopted.

online_residual_frequency_layer.construction: Engineering online-quantile wrapper around the existing continuation box. Before each run multiply the past-only base radius by scalar q_t. After observing the completed-run normalized continuation diagnostic d_t, form score max_i |d_t-center_pre,i|/base_radius_i and update q by pinball SGD toward tau=0.9 with step 0.8/sqrt(t), clipped to [0.5,4]. This is an engineering analog of online quantile/conformal calibration, not an implementation of any cited theorem.
online_residual_frequency_layer.selection: Step-size family selected on a disjoint discovery seed family; the numbers below are one-shot validation on 12 new streams/scenario.
online_residual_frequency_layer.interpretation: The frequency layer greatly improved gradual post-hoc true-A box coverage on this validation set (0.6653 for raw uncertainty to 0.9417) and achieved about 0.90 diagnostic coverage there, but recurring exact allocation degraded beyond fixed beta and retained a 1.2948 worst transient. This cleanly separates calibration-frequency improvement from transient allocation safety. No one-step variance guarantee is claimed.

derived_results.claim: A smooth exponential genealogy-disagreement cap generalizes better than the r126 hard cooldown on some averages, but does not robustly dominate fixed beta=0.5. In fresh recurring validation it had mean ratio 0.87846 and worst 1.17002 versus 0.87634 and 1.08831 for fixed beta=0.5.

An observable online continuation-residual quantile layer can substantially improve frequency-style box coverage under gradual drift, yet still leave large recurring transients. Better calibration of its own residual object is therefore not a substitute for a run-level allocation-risk certificate.

The UAI 2026 certificate-driven calibration pattern provides a stronger cross-field design motif: retain a fixed defensive backbone and allow a corrective/aggressive component only when a predictable martingale-style certificate supports it, with outcomes used only on subsequent rounds. Transferring this motif to particle allocation requires a certificate for an observable proxy whose relation to allocation variance is itself controlled.

The targeted search again did not establish a theorem-clean single-run generation-wise variance estimator specifically for the independent-stratified multi-generation particle filter. This is a search result, not a nonexistence claim.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The continuous genealogy-risk controller was selected from a finite synthetic discovery grid and failed to robustly beat the fixed defensive reserve on disjoint recurring validation; it is not an adoption candidate.

The online residual-scale wrapper is an engineering online-quantile controller, not a theorem-equivalent implementation of DtACI, strongly-adaptive conformal prediction, or online conformal optimization.
Diagnostic-frequency coverage and post-hoc true-A box coverage are different objects. Neither observed frequency establishes one-step containment of true A.
The synthetic Feynman-Kac results do not imply real-agent or AGI performance gains.
No genealogy theorem was transferred from another resampling scheme to independent stratified resampling.
frontier: Abandon the simple exponential argmax-genealogy risk map as an adoption candidate. Preserve genealogy only as a localizer/covariate, not a direct concentration control.

Construct a certificate-gated defensive-backbone controller: fixed beta=0.5 is the always-available backbone; an aggressive uncertainty allocation is a corrective proposal. Define a bounded observable completed-run loss or residual for the correction and derive a predictable martingale/confidence-sequence gate before allowing concentration on subsequent runs. Keep the theorem scope on the observable proxy separate from true variance unless a bridge bound is proved.

Use online conformal/online-quantile machinery only for the calibration object it actually covers. Compare local/strongly-adaptive calibration for residual-frequency behavior, but do not infer per-run variance safety from it.
Continue targeted theorem search for independent-stratified single-run generation-wise variance estimation and for confidence sequences under dependent stratified particle clouds.
After a certificate-gated controller is stable, extend to 20 generations and add a terminal-generation boundary diagnostic.
exact_next_action: Define the defensive backbone q0 from beta=0.5 and the aggressive proposal q1 from the existing uncertainty controller. From completed-run continuation diagnostics only, construct a bounded paired proxy-loss difference whose conditional mean can be monitored predictably. Derive an anytime-valid one-sided martingale/confidence-sequence gate for whether q1 is better than q0 on that proxy; allow q1 or a continuous blend only after certification, and immediately retain q0 as fallback. Test abrupt/gradual/recurring drift on discovery streams, freeze the gate, then validate once on disjoint streams. Separately quantify how often proxy certification agrees with the post-hoc exact A allocation ordering; unless that bridge is itself certified, label the gate as proxy-safe rather than variance-safe.
